I maybe can have also the useMediaTimeline in the @src/screens/room/fragments/room-timeline/RoomTimeline.tsx . Find the best approach.  THis is how element x does it:
How the two timelines work together
Tapping media doesn't reuse the room's timeline — it spins up a second, parallel timeline that's filtered to only media events, and hands that to the preview. The room timeline keeps running in the background so you can come back to it.

The handoff from room → preview
When the user taps an image/video, TimelineInteractionHandler.mediaPreviewAction decides which timeline the preview gets:

Source timeline kind	What preview uses
.live (normal room)	New filtered timeline, focus .live
.detached (focused on a specific event)	New filtered timeline, focus .eventID(…)
.pinned (pinned messages screen)	New filtered timeline, focus .pinned
.media / .thread (already filtered)	Reuse active
For the common case (line 602) it calls timelineControllerFactory.buildMessageFilteredTimelineController(...) with allowedMessageTypes: [.image, .video] (or [.audio, .file]), wraps the result in a fresh TimelineViewModel, and passes that to TimelineMediaPreviewViewModel. From that moment on, the preview has its own view model — its own paginator, its own state — independent of the room timeline.

How it gets "all the media"
It doesn't load all media upfront. The Rust SDK exposes filtered timelines as a first-class feature: JoinedRoomProxy.messageFilteredTimeline calls room.timelineWithConfiguration(...) with filter: .onlyMessage(types: [...]). The Rust side does the filtering server-side/store-side — the iOS app just gets a timeline that only ever contains media events, with the usual paginate-backwards/forwards primitives.

The preview then treats that stream the same way the room screen treats its own timeline: it observes timelineState.itemViewStates (TimelineMediaPreviewViewModel.swift:60-65) and triggers pagination when the user swipes to an edge (line 134-147).

The padding trick in the data source
TimelineMediaPreviewDataSource exists to work around a QLPreviewController quirk: calling reloadData() always reloads the current item, destroying zoom/playback/scroll state. So they can't just feed QuickLook a growing array.

Instead:

numberOfPreviewItems returns previewItems.count + backwardPadding + forwardPadding — starting at 100 slots on each side (line 40).
When pagination delivers N new items on one side, they decrement that side's padding by N (lines 87-88) instead of growing the array.
The net count stays constant, so QL never reloads — the current item's index doesn't move.
previewController(_:previewItemAt:) (line 129): indices inside [firstPreviewItemIndex, lastPreviewItemIndex] return a real media item; indices past the edges return one of four Loading sentinels (paginatingBackwards, paginatingForwards, timelineStart, timelineEnd) that QL renders as blanks while the preview VM kicks off pagination.
The comment at line 98-106 is candid about the tradeoffs ("I hate QLPreviewController!") — redacted items mid-view can't be removed without blowing up the current-item state, so they're ignored.

The return trip
Picking "View in timeline" from the preview menu sends .viewInRoomTimeline(itemID) up through RoomFlowCoordinator, which fires .presentRoom(presentationAction: .eventFocus(...)). The room screen then asks the Rust SDK for a detached, event-focused timeline (filter: .all, focus: .event(eventId:, numContextEvents: 100, …)) and auto-scrolls to that event — a third timeline variant, distinct from both the live room timeline and the media-filtered one.

Shared with the Media Gallery
The same TimelineMediaPreviewViewModel is used by the dedicated MediaEventsTimelineScreen gallery. The gallery runs two always-on filtered timelines (media + files) via the same buildMessageFilteredTimelineController, and when you tap a tile there it hands the already-filtered timeline straight to the preview — that's the .media case that hits break at line 594 and reuses the active timeline.

## Summary — Media Viewer refactor

### Core idea
Replaced two separate image/video modals with a single swipeable `MediaViewerModal` that owns its own media-filtered timeline — matching Element X's pattern. Plain-URI avatar viewing stays in the old `ImageViewerModal`.

### New files
- [`MediaViewerModal.tsx`](src/shared/components/media-viewer-modal/MediaViewerModal.tsx) — 10-line atom-read shell; renders nothing when closed so the hook never mounts.
- [`MediaViewerModalContent.tsx`](src/shared/components/media-viewer-modal/MediaViewerModalContent.tsx) — full viewer; owns its filtered timeline via `useMediaTimeline`.
- [`MediaImagePage.tsx`](src/shared/components/media-viewer-modal/MediaImagePage.tsx) — per-page `ImageZoom` with encrypted-image caching.
- [`MediaVideoPage.tsx`](src/shared/components/media-viewer-modal/MediaVideoPage.tsx) — per-page `react-native-video`, only loads/plays when the page is active.
- [`MediaEdgePage.tsx`](src/shared/components/media-viewer-modal/MediaEdgePage.tsx) — black full-screen loading sentinel.
- [`utils.ts`](src/shared/components/media-viewer-modal/utils.ts) — `getMediaKind`, `getImageContent`, `getVideoContent` helpers.

### Swipe UX
- Horizontal `inverted` FlashList with `pagingEnabled` — index 0 (newest) renders at the right, swipe right → older items.
- `initialScrollIndex` + seeded `currentIndex` so the tapped event is visible immediately; a fallback `scrollToIndex` runs once the filtered timeline hydrates and resolves the real index.
- Header (sender/date/info) only shows for event pages.

### Pagination fix (the critical one)
The eager `while (!reachedStart) paginateBackwards(100)` loop in [`useMediaTimeline`](src/screens/room-media/hooks/useMediaTimeline.ts) was dragging the shared room store to the start of history and flooding [`useRoomTimeline`](src/modules/timeline/hooks/useRoomTimeline.ts). Fixed by:
- Replacing the loop with a single initial `paginateBackwards(PAGE_SIZE)` and exposing `loadMore()` + `reachedStart`.
- Removing the `useMediaTimeline` mount from [`RoomTimeline`](src/screens/room/fragments/room-timeline/RoomTimeline.tsx) — the viewer now owns its own timeline, only mounted while open.
- Wiring `loadMore` through [`MediaList`](src/screens/room-media/fragments/media-list/MediaList.tsx) / [`FilesList`](src/screens/room-media/fragments/files-list/FilesList.tsx) via `onEndReached` so the gallery grid paginates on scroll instead of upfront.
- In the viewer, an effect triggers `loadMore` exactly when the user lands on the older-edge sentinel.

### Edge sentinel
- Pages array is `[...events, olderEdgeSentinel]`. No newer-side sentinel — new items arrive live via the timeline listener.
- Sentinel always shows a spinner.
- When the user lands on it with `reachedStart=true`, a 500 ms timer fires a one-time toast ("No older media") and `scrollToIndex` snaps back to the last event.
- While still paginating (`!reachedStart`), the spinner stays; real items fill in as they arrive.

### Payload + atoms
- Added `mediaViewerPayload` = `{ roomId, initialEventId, initialEvent }` in [timeline.d.ts](src/@types/timeline.d.ts). `initialEvent` seeds the first frame before hydration.
- Deleted `videoViewerPayload` atom and the whole `video-viewer-modal/` folder.
- Updated `ImageMessage`, `VideoMessage`, `MediaGallery`, `ImageInfoBottomSheet`, `VideoInfoBottomSheet` to use the new payload; info sheets now close `mediaViewerPayload` on reply/forward/delete.
- `imageViewerPayload` stayed for the three avatar callers (Profile, UserProfile, RoomDetails); `ImageViewerModal` was simplified to avatar-only (no event/info code).

### Result
Swipeable image+video viewer with lazy pagination that no longer floods the room timeline, plus a proper end-of-history UX (spinner → toast → snap back).
